approach:
Recognise the limit once, where the driver reply becomes an AgentOutput, and carry it as typed data. (1) claude.rs: a pure `parse_usage_limit(text, now)` returns the reset Timestamp when the text matches "hit your ... limit ... resets <Mon D, H[:MM]am/pm> (UTC)". `output_from_result` uses it only when the result has no model usage, and returns `InvocationOutcome::Limited` (new variant in records.rs), cost `Some(0.0)`, zero usage with `usage_measured: false`, empty `models_used`, and the reply text in `detail`. `AgentOutput` stays unchanged, so athena-agent/src/lib.rs is not touched. A second pure function in claude.rs, `usage_limit_reset(detail, now)`, is the one place the reset time is read from that text. It is called only when the outcome is already `Limited`, and only in `invoke_and_record`. (2) records.rs: `Invocation.limit_resets_at: Option<Timestamp>` (serde default, skipped when None). A Limited record has reported cost 0 and empty `models_used`, so `check_invocation` passes with no gate change. (3) athena-core: `invoke_and_record` stores `limit_resets_at` on the record and writes one global hold file when a Limited output has a parseable reset. disk.rs holds `USAGE_LIMIT = "environment: usage limit"`, the hold helpers, and an `is_environment_reason` extension so the candidate is kept and `athena retry` resumes. Each model-call stage (reading, planning, critic, producer, verifier) tests `outcome == Limited` before its generic failure branch. The stage returns a typed `UsageLimit { resets_at: Option<Timestamp> }` in its result beside the existing reason text. (4) drain: `Read` and `Run` gain `limited`, set from the typed field. `run_job` handles it before the failure branches and returns a new `RunStep::Limited` / `ItemEnd::Limited`. `finish` calls `set_stop(Stop::UsageLimit, ..)` without touching `failures`. The label is "usage limit" and the report carries the reset time. (5) status.rs: `StatusView.usage_limit`, read from the hold and shown only while the reset is after `now`. display.rs and main.rs print the stop and the status line. (6) CHANGELOG entry.

Revision answers: finding 1: criterion 8 now has a `fails_without`. Finding 2: athena-agent/src/lib.rs is dropped from the plan; the typed carrier is the new outcome variant plus the record field, not a new `AgentOutput` field. Finding 3: crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs is kept as a test-only file, with the reason under decision 6 and a fallback in open_questions.

decisions.choice: Add `InvocationOutcome::Limited`, set in `claude::output_from_result` via `parse_usage_limit`. Do not add a field to `AgentOutput` (lib.rs stays untouched). The reset time reaches the record through `claude::usage_limit_reset(detail, ended_at)` in `invoke_and_record`, which runs only for a Limited output.
decisions.reason: Root cause: the limit reply is parsed in the driver layer and today becomes an `Error` with free text, so every stage counts it as a failure. Recognising it once there fixes all five stages. The typed outcome is the signal; stages, drain and status read the outcome, the record field and the hold, never reason text. Avoiding a lib.rs edit keeps the change inside the listed deliverables.

rejected.why: Cleaner carrier, but lib.rs is outside the listed deliverables (finding 2) and the same information is derivable from the outcome plus detail. If the reviewer prefers the field, it is a one-line addition (see open_questions).

rejected.option: Match 'usage limit' text in drain.rs or in each stage
rejected.why: This is the per-stage patch and the text parsing criterion 6 forbids.

rejected.option: Keep outcome Error and add a detail prefix
rejected.why: The record would not be limited and the failure paths would still fire.

decisions.choice: Zero cost is reported cost 0.0 with empty `models_used` and lower-bound zero tokens (`usage_measured: false`).
decisions.reason: `check_invocation` compares costs only when `models_used` is non-empty and checks measured tokens only against `models_used`, so the record passes with the gate's rules unchanged.

rejected.option: Measured zero tokens with a models_used entry
rejected.why: Invents usage the model never reported.
Out of scope: the gate's rules for other records stay unchanged.

decisions.choice: Reuse the `environment:` reason family: add `environment: usage limit` and extend `is_environment_reason`.
decisions.reason: The candidate-keeping and retry path already exists for low disk, so the job stays retryable and keeps its candidate with the smallest change. Drain decides on the typed `limited` field, never on this text.

rejected.option: A new job state for limited jobs
rejected.why: Touches many records and gate rules for no gain over the reason prefix.

decisions.choice: One global hold file in the state dir (reset time), written by `invoke_and_record`, read by `status()` and shown only while the reset is after `now`. If the reset cannot be parsed, record the limited invocation but write no hold.
decisions.reason: A usage limit belongs to the account, not a job. Hiding it after the reset needs no cleanup. Inventing a reset time would be worse than showing none.

rejected.why: One account-wide condition would show as one line per job.

decisions.choice: Drain ends with a new `Stop::UsageLimit` and never uses the item-failure path; the item stays queued.
decisions.reason: Criterion 3 needs the stop reason 'usage limit' naming the reset time and an unchanged failure counter, for both the reading and run steps.

rejected.option: Treat it as `ItemEnd::Held` and keep draining
rejected.why: Every later item would hit the same limit; the loop should stop.

decisions.choice: Put the two end-to-end drain tests (reading step and run step) and the ordinary-error drain test in the existing crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs. Unit tests with a Stub `Steps` go in src/drain.rs.
decisions.reason: tests/drain.rs holds the only harness that runs `RealSteps` with a fake driver against a real repository (see the low-disk tests near lines 1541-1790). A new harness in src/drain.rs would duplicate it. It is a test file, not governance, and the change to it is test-only.

rejected.option: Only Stub-`Steps` unit tests in src/drain.rs
rejected.why: They would not exercise `RealSteps` filling `Read.limited` and `Run.limited` from the real stage results, so a break in that mapping would pass.

rejected.option: Build a new RealSteps harness inside src/drain.rs tests
rejected.why: Duplicates a large fixture for the sake of file-count.

risks.risk: New `Invocation` field and `InvocationOutcome::Limited` break struct literals and exhaustive matches across crates.
risks.mitigation: Serde default on the field so old records load. Let the compiler find every site; run `cargo clippy --all-targets`.

risks.risk: A false positive turns an ordinary reply that mentions a limit into a hold.
risks.mitigation: Recognise only a result with no model usage whose text matches both 'hit your ... limit' and 'resets'. Negative tests: an ordinary error and a successful reply that quotes the phrase.

risks.risk: The reset text has no year and names a zone, so it can be mis-parsed.
risks.mitigation: Parse UTC only, infer the next occurrence at or after `now`, and test with a fixed `now` including year rollover. Any other format leaves the reset None: the record is still Limited and no hold is written.

risks.risk: The fake driver and the real driver diverge.
risks.mitigation: The fake routes the reply text through the same claude.rs function. Criterion 1 exercises the real driver through the stand-in script.

risks.risk: A stage still counts the limit as a failure because the generic failure branch comes first.
risks.mitigation: Check Limited first in every non-success branch; one test per stage; the ordinary-error test (criterion 5) runs beside them.

risks.risk: Deriving the reset from `detail` in `invoke_and_record` is a second read of the reply text.
risks.mitigation: It runs only for an already-Limited output, uses the same claude.rs parser, and stores the result as the typed record field, so stages, drain and status never read text.

demonstrations.method: Test through the real driver. In claude.rs `stand_in_tests`, add a `MODE=limit` branch to the existing shell stand-in script. It emits a `system` init line, then a `result` line with `is_error` true, result text "You've hit your weekly limit · resets Oct 29, 6pm (UTC)", empty `modelUsage` and zero usage. The test calls `ClaudeCodeDriver::invoke` through the existing `driver(...)` helper (which sets `refuse_nested_runs: false`), with the existing `spec(...)` and `Recorder`. Both seams exist today; the new pieces are the `limit` mode in the script, `parse_usage_limit` and `usage_limit_reset`. A pure test calls `parse_usage_limit(text, now)` with a fixed `now` of 2026-10-28 and expects 2026-10-29T18:00:00Z. A second pure test uses a `now` after the date to check the year rollover. Negative tests: a reply with model usage, and an ordinary error text, are not limits.
demonstrations.observes: The driver output has `outcome == Limited`, `cost_usd == Some(0.0)`, zero usage and `usage_measured == false`. `usage_limit_reset(detail, ended_at)` gives 18:00 UTC on Oct 29. The pure test gives the exact timestamp for the fixed `now`. The negative cases are not Limited.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without recognition in `output_from_result` the outcome stays `Error`, so the `Limited` assertion fails. Without the parser the reset is None, so the timestamp assertion (month, day, hour, minute) fails. Without the zero cost the `Some(0.0)` assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: One test per stage, each driving the real stage entry point against `FakeAgentDriver::new(script)`. The script returns a `FakeTurn` carrying the limit reply text for that stage's `Role`. The fake has no limit logic: it passes the text through `claude::output_from_result`/`parse_usage_limit`, the same code the real driver uses. Reading uses `read_request` in reading.rs. Planner, critic, producer and verifier use `Athena::go` (run/mod.rs) with the fixtures that already build an `Athena` with a fake driver in run/mod.rs tests. The seam `FakeAgentDriver::new(Script)` exists today; step 4 adds the optional reply-text field to `FakeTurn` in fake.rs. Each test loads the invocation record from the state files or the closing result, then asserts: `outcome == Limited`; reported cost 0.0; `check_invocation(...)` returns no violations; an `AnyRecord` JSON round trip; the stage result carries the typed limit; the closing reason is `environment: usage limit` and `is_environment_reason` accepts it; no failure reason is recorded; and, for producer and verifier, the candidate still exists and `resumable_stop` is true so `athena retry` accepts the job.
demonstrations.observes: For the five stages: Limited, zero-cost, gate-clean records, a typed limit on the stage result, the job retryable with its candidate kept, and no failure counted.
demonstrations.fails_without: If a stage keeps the generic `outcome != Success` branch, reading returns `ReadError::Failed` and planner, critic, producer and verifier close with a work-failure reason. The typed-limit and `environment: usage limit` assertions then fail. If the record were not Limited or not zero cost, the Limited or `check_invocation` assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: Two end-to-end tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs, in the style of the existing low-disk `RealSteps` tests (around lines 1541-1790), which already run `RealSteps` with a fake driver on a real repository. Test A: the script returns the limit reply for `Role::Reader` on a queued item. Test B: the reading succeeds and the script returns it for `Role::Producer`. Each calls the production drain entry those tests use, then asserts `report.stop == Stop::UsageLimit`, the label 'usage limit', that the rendered stop line names the reset time, `report.usage_limit` is set, there is no failed item, the failure count is unchanged, and the fake driver was called once for the item. Unit tests in src/drain.rs use a Stub `Steps` with `limited` set to check the loop makes no second attempt and leaves `failures` alone. The harness exists today; step 8 adds `Read.limited`, `Run.limited`, `Stop::UsageLimit` and `Report.usage_limit`.
demonstrations.observes: The stop is 'usage limit' with the reset time, not 'repeated failure'. The failure counter and failed-item are unchanged. One attempt is made. Both the reading step and the run step behave this way.
demonstrations.fails_without: If drain mapped the limit onto the failure path, the report would stop with 'repeated failure' or the failure count would rise, failing the `Stop::UsageLimit`, label and failures-unchanged assertions.

demonstrations.method: status.rs tests using the existing status fixture. Write the hold with the new `disk` helper, resetting after `now`; call `status()` and render with `display::status`. Then write a hold whose reset is before `now` and call again. A pure view function that takes `now` explicitly is also tested, so no clock is mocked. The fixture exists today; step 5 adds the helpers and `StatusView.usage_limit`.
demonstrations.observes: While holding, `view.usage_limit` is Some and the rendered text contains 'usage limit' and the reset time. After the reset time, `view.usage_limit` is None and the text contains neither.
demonstrations.fails_without: If `status()` ignored the hold, the 'shown while holding' assertion fails. If it ignored the reset time, a stale limit would still show and the 'after reset' assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: The script returns a `FakeTurn` with `outcome: Error` and `detail: Some("boom")` (no limit text) for `Role::Reader`. A core test calls `read_request`; a drain test in tests/drain.rs attempts the same item twice through the RealSteps harness. Both use seams that exist today.
demonstrations.observes: The invocation record has `outcome == Error`. The reading result carries the error text with no typed limit. The failure counter rises, and drain stops with 'repeated failure' naming the item.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the new branch caught every error, or reading stopped returning `ReadError::Failed`, the record would not be Error and the failure count would not rise, so the assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: Run the three checks Athena runs on the result as whole commands. They include the existing `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` budget test and the records round-trip tests that cover the new optional `limit_resets_at` field.
demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
demonstrations.observes: All three exit 0: formatting is clean, there are no clippy warnings, and every test passes, including the new limit tests and all existing tests.
demonstrations.fails_without: Missed constructor updates for the new `Invocation` field, a non-exhaustive match on `InvocationOutcome` or `Stop`, an unformatted file or any failing new test makes one of the three commands exit non-zero.

open_questions: How the reading result and the finished-run result carry the typed limit is not settled; I did not read those struct definitions. A new field on each beside `reader_error` and the reason is the plan, kept minimal.
Which existing run/mod.rs and tests/drain.rs fixtures build an `Athena` with a fake driver for the planner, critic, producer and verifier was not read. The producer must reuse them.

If the reviewer prefers a typed `AgentOutput.limit` field to the detail re-read, it needs a one-line change in athena-agent/src/lib.rs, which is outside the listed deliverables. This plan keeps lib.rs untouched.

If crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs must stay out of the change, criterion 3 falls back to Stub unit tests in drain.rs plus a pure mapping function for the `RealSteps` fill. That gives weaker evidence for the real mapping.
When the reset is not UTC or cannot be parsed, no hold is written, so status shows nothing and the drain stop says the reset time is unknown. A fallback hold duration would be a separate decision.
Whether a second drain should refuse to start while a hold with a future reset stands is left out because no criterion asks for it.
Whether anything beyond `cargo test` enumerates `Stop::ALL` (docs checks) was not searched.
